Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

>     * `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes

>     * `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

>

#!/bin/bash
# ==========================================
# Configuración de Entorno
# ==========================================
export PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True,garbage_collection_threshold:0.2
export FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_SIZE=1073741824
export VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE=1073741824
export VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  # ← necesario para 262144 tokens

# Persistencia de kernels Triton (CRUCIAL para no recompilar tras reiniciar)
export TRITON_CACHE_DIR="/home/jaime/.triton_cache"
mkdir -p "$TRITON_CACHE_DIR"

# ==========================================
# Parámetros del Modelo
# ==========================================
MODEL_PATH="/home/jaime/Modelos/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ/"
CHAT_TEMPLATE="/home/jaime/Modelos/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ/chat_template.jinja"
SERVED_NAME="qwen3.6-27b-awq-marlin"
# --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_next_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \

echo "Iniciando vLLM en segundo plano..."

# ==========================================
# Ejecución del Servidor vLLM
# ==========================================
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --chat-template "$CHAT_TEMPLATE" \
    --model "$MODEL_PATH" \
    --served-model-name "$SERVED_NAME" \
    --max-num-seqs 10 \
    --max-model-len 132144  \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --override-generation-config '{"thinking": false}' \
    --quantization marlin \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --override-generation-config '{"thinking":	 false}' \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000
   
# Capturamos el PID del servidor vLLM
VLLM_PID=$!

# ==========================================
# Fase de Monitoreo y Warmup Activo (CORREGIDO)
# ==========================================
echo "Esperando a que el endpoint de vLLM esté disponible..."

# Cambiado a GET (-X GET) y validando el código de estado HTTP internamente
until [ "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://192.168.1.10:8000/health)" -eq 200 ]; do
    sleep 3
done

echo "¡vLLM online (HTTP 200)! Enviando Dummy Request pesado para forzar JIT de Triton..."
echo "Esto compilará los kernels de MROPE, Marlin y PagedAttention ahora mismo."

# El Dummy Request con n=3 y prompt denso
curl -s -X POST "http://192.168.1.10:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "'"$SERVED_NAME"'",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Warmup initialization sequence. Triggering causal convolutions, mrope position matrix alignments, and paged memory allocation for context blocks. Ensure all Triton cache misses are handled immediately."}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 30,
    "n": 3
  }' > /dev/null

echo "--------------------------------------------------------"
echo "Warmup completado con éxito. Servidor listo para producción."
echo "Los picos de latencia de Triton se han resuelto."
echo "--------------------------------------------------------"

# Mantiene el script de bash vinculado al proceso de vLLM
wait $VLLM_PID

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #23903: Same "Failed to send prompt. Unable to retrieve session" error reported in the Web UI — same error message and symptom
- #30333: Session list disappears / gets stuck after switching projects on Windows Desktop — very similar root cause (sessions not visible after switching projects, full restart required to recover)

This is exactly the kind of bug that makes people think the model is the expensive part when the real problem is the loop policy. The useful split is usually by failure class: transient, deterministic, permission, verifier, and unknown. Only one of those deserves automatic retries. The rest should stop early with a receipt so the parent agent does not keep buying the same mistake again. We ended up building MartinLoop around that exact boundary after seeing retry loops become the most expensive part of agent work.

## Data dump: 5× SIGABRT in 20h, ~15 GB core dumps, WSL2 + Bun + 1.15.13

Environment and crash signature only. I am not proposing a fix.

### Environment

- opencode-ai@1.15.13 (npm, Bun runtime)
- WSL2, kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- Running mode: `opencode web --port 4096 --hostname 127.0.0.1` for several hours
- Provider: configured (working)
- Plugin: `oh-my-opencode` (installed)
- Working dir when the crash happened: a Node project (`ParParPar`) running `npm test`
- Accreted state at crash: `opencode.db` 1.85 GB, `snapshot/` 914 MB, `worktree/` 780 MB, `storage/session_diff/` 257 MB (2384 files, one is 63 MB), `tool-output/` 63 MB

### Crash signature

`opencode.exe: opencode: potentially unexpected fatal signal 6.`

(WSL2 wording, signal 6 = SIGABRT, no libc "abort message" → killed via `tgkill(pid, pid, SIGABRT)` from somewhere inside the process — not from libc `abort()` and not from the kernel OOM killer.)

5 SIGABRTs in 20 hours. Each leaves a 15–17 GB WSL crash dump in
`C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\wsl-crash-*` named like
`wsl-crash-<unix-ts>-<pid>-_home_<user>_.nvm_versions_node_v22.22.2_lib_node_modules_opencode-ai_bin_opencode.exe-6.dmp`.

The `-6` in the filename is the signal number. The leading PID matches the live `opencode.exe` PID reported by `pgrep`.

The most recent crash happened roughly 14 minutes after a fresh `opencode web` restart, while the agent was running `timeout 900 npm test` in the bash tool against the ParPar project.

### Strings found inside the dmesg memory dump of the crashed process

This is the part that points at a code path. The dmesg `/dev/kmsg` snapshot
dumped at crash time contains these literal strings in the dying process's
memory:

- `Buffer.allocUnsafe`  → present in `lib/bufferpool.js:4` of the ParPar project (`var allocBuffer = (Buffer.allocUnsafe || Buffer)`)
- `gf64_solve`  → symbol from a native `.node` addon ParPar loads for PAR3 repair
- A reference to `par2`-style Reed-Solomon code paths

**Implication:** the opencode process's *own* memory contained the text of `lib/bufferpool.js` and the name of a native addon's exported function. The opencode binary does not have these strings — they were loaded into the parent's address space at runtime. The most likely vehicle is the snapshot/file-watcher pipeline reading file contents from the working dir, but I have not confirmed this.

### What I tried to reproduce

I tried three variants on a **clean** WSL2 install (no `oh-my-opencode`, no
prior sessions, no MCP, ~27 GB free RAM) with opencode-ai@1.15.13:

1. `opencode run` with a 50 MB bash-tool output (1 MB/s of `A`s for 50 s).
2. `opencode run` with a 500 MB bash-tool output.
3. `opencode web` (port 4097) + `opencode run --attach` with a 500 MB bash-tool output.

None of them crashed. All three peaked at <700 MB RSS and exited cleanly. The
bash tool correctly offloaded the output to a file at 50 KB and the
`metadata.output` field was capped at ~30 KB (a trailing preview).

This rules out the simplest theory, "large bash-tool output kills the parent
process". The bash tool's own internal buffers are well-bounded:

- `list: Chunk[]` is a sliding window capped at `maxBytes * 2` = 100 KB
  (`packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:495-510`)
- `full` is offloaded to a file when it crosses `maxBytes` = 50 KB
  (`packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:516-525`)
- `last = preview(last + chunk)` is capped at `MAX_METADATA_LENGTH` = 30 000
  chars by `preview()` (`packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:223-226`,
  `truncate.ts` constants `MAX_LINES = 2000`, `MAX_BYTES = 50 * 1024`)

The full stream consumer in `shell.ts` runs in a `Stream.runForEach` inside
`Effect.forkScoped`, which does await `handle.exitCode` first, so it should
drain the child's stdout before the function returns.

### Where I think the actual leak is (hypothesis, not confirmed)

Turns out this was the #29581 bug — old sessions had empty path fields, so the TUI session query filtered them out.
Closure:
- #29581 was the root cause (path filter mismatch for home-sourced sessions).
- Applied the DB workaround locally: UPDATE session SET path = substr(directory, 2) WHERE path IS NULL OR path = ''; — backfilled path from directory for 47 orphaned sessions. All 91 sessions now visible in TUI.
- This is effectively a duplicate of #29581 (already fixed by PR #29582).
Closing as resolved.

I investigated and prepared a focused fix for this.

Root cause confirmed
- Config/skill discovery uses glob scans rooted at `.opencode/` with recursive patterns (`**/*.md`, `**/SKILL.md`) and follows symlinks.
- Those scans did not exclude `node_modules`, so once dependencies are installed in `.opencode/node_modules`, discovery walks huge trees and startup can stall.

Fix implemented
- Added `ignore` support to core glob wrapper (`packages/core/src/util/glob.ts`) so callers can pass exclusion patterns.
- Applied `ignore: ["**/node_modules/**"]` to discovery scans used by:
  - agents (`packages/opencode/src/config/agent.ts`)
  - commands (`packages/opencode/src/config/command.ts`)
  - plugins (`packages/opencode/src/config/plugin.ts`)
  - skills (`packages/opencode/src/skill/index.ts`)

- `packages/opencode/test/util/glob.test.ts`
  - new test: `supports ignore patterns`
- `packages/opencode/test/config/config.test.ts`

- `packages/opencode/test/skill/skill.test.ts`

  - `session.processor strips MiniMax trailing tool_call leak suffix from assistant text`
  - Verifies assistant text ends as clean `Answer` instead of leaked marker suffix.

Root cause confirmed in `SessionCompaction.process`: when the processor leaves `assistantMessage.error` without a terminal `finish`, compaction can stop without marking the summary as terminal.

That leaves an errored summary in a non-final state and can be interpreted as pending work on later loops.

I pushed a fix that normalizes this branch to terminal state: if `processor.message.error` is set and `finish` is missing, we now set `finish: "error"`, persist the message, and then stop.

I also added a regression test that simulates a processor returning with `error` but no `finish`, and verifies the summary ends with `finish=error`.

Validation run from `packages/opencode`:

- `bun typecheck`
- `bun test test/session/compaction.test.ts -t "sets finish=error when processor reports summary error without terminal finish"`
- `bun test test/session/compaction.test.ts`
